Class CustomContainerMenu

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.menu.CustomContainerMenu
public class CustomContainerMenu extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu
A custom container menu: its created slots, its panels as the server knows them, and whether each is shown (§0067). Built by SlotLayout (builder(MenuType)); shift-click routes through QuickMoveRouter.

A proper subclass of AbstractContainerMenu: vanilla's sync machinery walks this.slots, and anything that breaks instanceof Slot breaks the world. It runs on both sides with the same declaration, so both build the same slots in the same order.

What it does not hold

How a panel looks (its elements, style, placement, toggle key) is MenuKit's client Panel, declared on the client with ClientMenu.of(menu).panel(id, ...) and built by the screen. This class names no client type, so it builds on a dedicated server.

Panel visibility is the server's

Whether a panel is shown is server state, synced to the client by one vanilla DataSlot per panel. setPanelVisible(String, boolean) is called on the server; the client follows. A player may ask to show or hide only a panel declared SlotLayout.PanelBuilder.toggleable() (vanilla's clickMenuButton); any other request is refused. A hidden panel's slots are inert: they read empty and refuse placement and pickup, on both sides.

Right clicks

A right click on a shown slot whose group has a SlotLayout.PanelBuilder.rightClick(BiConsumer) handler runs the handler instead of vanilla's click. It is a click like any other: the client runs it as its prediction and sends it, and the server runs it too, which is the run that counts (§0067). Vanilla's take and put operations do not apply to it.

Validity

stillValid(Player) is real: the menu stays open while its validity holds, checked by vanilla on the server every tick. A CustomMenu sets it from CustomMenu.Builder.validWhen; without one the menu stays valid while the player is alive.
